newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp talks with Thyssen in good climate - source.
newsitem.headline: Krupp talks with Thyssen in good climate - source.

text.p: A source close to talks between German steel groups Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp and rival Thyssen AG to call of Krupp's hostile takeover bid in favour of a mutual venture have been progressing well, a source close to the talks said on Saturday.
"The talks are taking place in a good climate," the source told Reuters.
The chances appeared good that the two companies could reach a "letter of intent" by the negotiation deadline set for Thursday, the source said.

The talks so far have discussed that Thyssen, the larger of the two, would take over leadership of any venture between the two companies and their steel units -- Thyssen Steel AG and Krupp Hoesch Steel AG.
The talks came after Krupp launched a rare hostile bid for the larger Thyssen last week, offering Thyssen shareholders 435 marks a share, a 25 percent premium over the previous day's share price.

The takeover bid sparked a wave of labour unrest in the Ruhr area of Germany where the two groups are based and calls by German politicians, including Chancellor Helmut Kohl, for the groups to reach a deal that does not jeopardise jobs.
